picks.rationale: APEX gives LAD +0.5 a 59.7% probability of covering the first-five run line at the captured FanDuel price of -165, an established ELITE rating. Pregame starter data showed Chris Sale held a 5.2-point strikeout-minus-walk advantage over Yoshinobu Yamamoto; Chris Sale's fielding-independent run estimate was 1.04 runs lower than Yoshinobu Yamamoto's; Chris Sale carried a pitch-quality advantage of 15.6 points over Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Before issuance, Yoshinobu Yamamoto carried a 37.8% early-exit probability and Chris Sale a 59.4% probability; complete nine-hitter orders for both Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves were available, so neither lineup needed a fallback. The two fullest first-five scoring views centered Los Angeles Dodgers's margin at -0.34 and +0.48 runs, with typical spreads of 2.34 and 3.20 runs; they pointed in opposite directions, the outlook was broad, and their tail shapes were balanced or did not agree clearly. Across four baseball-based views, Los Angeles Dodgers's cover probability ranged from 54.9% to 64.0%, with 1 above, 3 below the 58.5% FanDuel baseline; the matchup evidence was internally split. Taken together, the starter, lineup, and scoring-shape evidence supported the measured move to the published 59.7% probability for LAD +0.5.

Taken together, the starter, lineup, and scoring-shape evidence supported the measured move to the published 55.2% probability for MIL +0.5.
